title: Pilot → Production: Traffic Gates & Owner Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This document is a pragmatic playbook and living tracker for pilots that are graduating to production. It focuses on traffic gating (phased ramp), the KPI thresholds that define each gate, owner responsibilities, and immediate runbook actions for abnormal signal detection. Use this as the canonical owner-facing checklist during pilot->production migrations for Redwood hosted and dedicated offerings.

Scope and usage notes:
- Scope: product-facing pilots where model endpoints (hosted/dedicated) will be exposed to more than 1,000 monthly active users or >5 RPS sustained.
- This is an operational product-ops artifact intended for cross-functional owners: PM, Eng, SRE, Solutions Eng, CS.
- Keep this doc live during the 6 weeks of ramp; snapshots of KPIs at each gate should be exported to the release epoch record.

Quick summary of gates:
- Gate 0: Internal validation (no external traffic). Criteria mostly engineering tests and smoke.
- Gate 1: Canary (1–5% of traffic or up to 1 RPS). Focus on correctness, latency P95, and basic error rates.
- Gate 2: Low ramp (5–25% traffic). Evaluate cost per 1k tokens, error trends, and user satisfaction signals.
- Gate 3: Scale (25–75%). Validate autoscaling behavior, KV cache hit rates, routing fallbacks.
- Gate 4: Production (>=75% or full). Final guardrails and SLA handoff.

Gate KPI sheet (owner, metric, measurement source, threshold, action if breached):
- Owner: PM (feature health), Eng (runtime), SRE (infrastructure), SE (customer signals), CS (support).

KPI lines:
1) User-facing errors (5xx or generation failures)
   - Owner: Eng/SRE
   - Source: Redwood Console error stream + Sentry/Jira alerts
   - Gate 1 threshold: <= 0.5% of requests; action: roll traffic back to previous model variant and page oncall if >1% sustained 5m
   - Gate 2 threshold: <= 0.3%; action: open incident, canary rollback, customer notifications if exposed

2) Latency (P95 generation latency)
   - Owner: Eng/Serving-runtime
   - Source: Redwood Console per-route latency histogram, distributed tracing
   - Gate 1 threshold: P95 <= 450ms; Gate 2: P95 <= 400ms; Gate 3: P95 <= 350ms
   - Action: enable lower-batch or smaller model variant, kick autoscale policy, notify PM

3) Cost per 1k tokens (unit economics)
   - Owner: Product Finance + PM
   - Source: Usage billing export + Console cost breakdown
   - Gate thresholds: cost drift <= 10% vs forecast; if >10% open budget review and enable quantization/limit features

4) Quality (automated eval pass rate on golden prompts + user satisfaction NPS/CS triage)
   - Owner: PM + Research/Applied ML
   - Source: Eval harness (CI) and customer support tags
   - Gate threshold: automated eval regression <= 1% absolute; human triage escalating if >3% of support tickets flagged as quality regressions

5) Cache efficiency (prefix/KV hit rate)
   - Owner: Serving-runtime Eng
   - Source: runtime telemetry + Console cache panels
   - Gate threshold: hit rate >= 60% for conversational use cases; if hit rate < 40% examine prompt patterns and caching config

6) Autoscaling stability (scale-up time and error impact)
   - Owner: SRE/Platform Eng
   - Source: Prometheus/Console autoscaler metrics
   - Gate threshold: scale-up within expected window (as defined in infra policy); if failure to scale triggers >1% error increase, revert to smaller traffic slice

Traffic ramping schedule (recommended baseline — adjust by customer size):
- Week -4 to -1: Internal validation, integration testing, security scan, IAM/KMS checks.
- Week 0 (Canary): 1% traffic for 48–72 hours. Continuous validation against KPIs.
- Week 1 (Low ramp): 5% for 3 days → 10% for 3 days. Focus on cost and error trend convergence.
- Week 2 (Mid ramp): 25% traffic for 5–7 days, stress autoscale scenarios at peak hour.
- Week 3 (High ramp): 50% traffic for 3–7 days, run a simulated SLO burn test.
- Week 4: Decision to go to production (>=75% or full) pending final stakeholder signoff and no unresolved criticals.

Owner matrix (single-line contact + immediate action):
- PM: Sanjay Patel (owner for go/no-go, product health, customer comms)
- Eng Lead: Elena Park (serving runtime changes, model variants, rollback)
body_continued: - SRE Lead: Darren Cho (autoscale policy, infra incidents)
body_continued_2: - Solutions Eng: Priya Nair (customer-specific mitigations and configs)
body_continued_3: - Customer Success: Zoe Martinez (support routing and proactive comms)
body_continued_4:
Pre-launch checklist (must be green before Gate 1):
- Security review complete (SAST/DAST scans) — security@redwood.com signoff
- Data residency and KMS configured for customer data paths
- Canary model pinned and previous stable model available as fallback
- Observability dashboards created and shared with oncall; alert thresholds documented
- Runbook with rollback steps tested in staging
- Support runbook and templated customer messages (high-latency, degraded-quality) prepared
- Billing and quota limits configured (soft and hard limits tested)

Launch day checklist (Gate 1 → Gate 2 transitions):
- Confirm measurement window start time and baseline traffic slice
- Confirm oncall rotations for 48–72h and secondary contacts available
- Start canary traffic, monitor live dashboards for first 15 min, 1h, 6h, 24h
- Verify trace-id sampling for suspected failures and logs linked to Sentry/Console
- Communicate internal status in #launch-ops Slack channel and update Confluence release page

Escalation ladder (fast path):
- If user-facing errors spike >1% sustained for 5 minutes: Eng rollback + page SRE + PM standby
- If latency P95 breaches gate threshold by >50ms for 15 minutes: SRE/Eng triage + consider traffic rollback or model variant switch
- If cost forecast deviates >20% in 24h window: PM + Finance review; consider throttles or temporary quota caps

Post-peak validation and handoff to run-the-business:
- After 7 days at >=50% with stable KPIs (errors, latency, cost within thresholds), schedule a Handoff Review. Deliverables for handoff:
  - Final KPI snapshot exports and annotated incidents
  - Known limitations and mitigations
  - Owners for ongoing SLOs and escalation contacts

Template tracker (copy into sheet for live tracking):
Columns: date, gate, traffic %, key-metrics (errors, latency P95, cost/1k tokens, cache hit), trend (up/down/flat), owner updates, blockers, action taken, snapshot link
Example row:
2025-02-12, Gate 1 (canary), 1%, errors 0.12%, latency P95 420ms, cost variance +3%, owner note: metrics stable, next step: expand to 5% on 2025-02-14, blocker: none, snapshot: CONFLUENCE:prodops/pilot-runbook#snapshot-20250212

Common gotchas and mitigation recipes (rapid reference):
- Symptom: sudden quality regressions after a tokenizer or prompt template tweak.
  - Quick mitigation: revert template, pin model variant, run selective golden-suite tests, inform customers.
- Symptom: high P95 during peak caused by batching interactions.
  - Mitigation: lower batch size, route sensitive low-latency calls to a lower-batch pool, enable fallback pool for best-effort responses.
- Symptom: sustained cost delta vs forecast due to unexpected long-context patterns.
  - Mitigation: apply conservative max token limits, enable prefix caching, set quota for heavy customers and schedule cost-review.

Notes for cross-team coordination:
- Use the Confluence release page as the single source-of-truth for KPI exports and snapshots. Link each daily snapshot to the tracker template row.
- Slack channel naming: #pilot-<feature>-ops during ramp; archive to #product-launches after handoff.
- For Dedicated/private customers, ensure legal/finance signoff on Reserved Capacity terms before Gate 2 expansion.

Action items (next 48 hours from snapshot):
- [PM] Confirm customer comms templates and staging message for potential rollbacks — Sanjay (due 2025-02-19)
- [Eng] Add cache telemetry panel to the shared dashboard; set alert if hit rate <45% — Elena (due 2025-02-18)
- [SRE] Validate autoscaler policy in canary region with a synthetic load test — Darren (due 2025-02-20)
- [SE] Rehearse customer-specific fallback with customer X — Priya (due 2025-02-21)
